breaking.headline: Wholesale inflation jumps 6.5%, highest since 2022
breaking.fact: October's Producer Price Index rose 0.3% from September, below the 0.4% forecast, but the year-over-year rate climbed to 6.5% — its highest since November 2022 — while core PPI held at 5.0% year over year; the print keeps a December Fed rate hike fully priced.

breaking.headline: Nvidia board approaches Arm's Rene Haas in CEO search
breaking.fact: The Financial Times reports Nvidia's board has approached Arm CEO Rene Haas — a former Nvidia executive — as a possible successor to Jensen Huang; the board says it is still selecting a search firm and has not formally engaged any candidate, calling speculation “premature.” Arm fell 5.4% Friday; Nvidia reports earnings Tuesday.

breaking.headline: Chip stocks sink as AMD falls nearly 9%
breaking.fact: AMD plunged 8.75% to $534.06 and the PHLX Semiconductor Index fell 3.43% as chip stocks gave back the week's rally; Broadcom dropped about 7% and Nvidia fell 2%, dragging the Nasdaq down 0.91%.

breaking.headline: Storm alert for Houston on Sunday
breaking.fact: FOX 26 has a Storm Alert for Sunday: widespread rain and storms are expected across Southeast Texas, with 2 to 4 inches of localized heavy rain, a 1-in-4 street-flooding risk and a 1-in-5 chance of a strong thunderstorm; spotty showers may develop late Saturday.

weekInBrief.headline: Stocks end the week higher despite Friday's slide
weekInBrief.body: The S&P 500 finished the week up 2.5% at 7,561.67, the Nasdaq up 2.3% at 25,136.27 and the Dow up 2.1% at 52,347.55, holding most of the week's gains even after Friday's chip-led slide on hot inflation data and Nvidia's leadership turmoil.

weekInBrief.headline: Bitcoin slides below $69,000 as risk assets retreat
weekInBrief.body: Bitcoin dropped to about $68,700 on Friday, down almost 4% in 24 hours, as the Nasdaq's slide and a strong dollar pressured risk assets; the token slipped below its 200-week moving average.

weekInBrief.headline: Copper slides to a four-month low
weekInBrief.body: Copper fell 1.4% Friday to $6.11 a pound, its weakest since early July, as rising Fed inflation worries weighed on industrial metals; crude has dropped about 20% since mid-September, a move not yet reflected in the backward-looking inflation data.

weekInBrief.headline: Oil ends the week lower despite the Hormuz spike
weekInBrief.body: Brent crude fell 2.3% on the week and WTI 2.1%, giving back only part of Monday's sharp drop despite a late-week jump on attacks against tankers in the Strait of Hormuz; the early-week slide and the IEA's call for a fourth-quarter surplus kept the rally in check.

items.headline: Latest from the Strait
items.body: The IEA said Friday the world oil market will be in surplus in the fourth quarter as Gulf exports return and 71 million barrels of emergency stock releases flow through February. CENTCOM says it has redirected more than 100 ships trying to violate the blockade and insists the strait is open, while analysts at ISW note there is no physical evidence Iran has re-mined the strait since CENTCOM cleared it in August — the recent strikes appear aimed at ships' engine rooms by drone and missile, with Tehran calling them mine strikes. The IRGC claimed Friday it destroyed a U.S. early-warning radar in Bahrain, a claim CENTCOM has not confirmed and which followed its dismissal of reports of U.S. war preparations as “pure speculation.” On oil, Kpler's tracking still shows Iranian crude loadings at zero since late August — the first zero month since tracking began in 2013 — while non-Iranian crude keeps moving, at about 7.3 million barrels a day through the strait in the week to October 28.

space.headline: Starship Flight 15 lifts off — but the booster catch is aborted
space.body: SpaceX's Starship Flight 15 lifted off from Starbase at 4:47 p.m. CT Friday after the FAA issued the launch license that same day, but the double-catch bid fell at the first hurdle: one engine failed to relight during the boostback burn and the Super Heavy catch was aborted, with Booster 22 diverted to a Gulf splashdown. Ship 42, named “Don't Panic,” reached space and was set to deploy 26 Starlink V3 satellites before a roughly 22-hour coast; the first-ever ship catch is still targeted for Saturday afternoon around 3:17 p.m. CT, if the ship passes its return checks.

space.headline: Evolution found another way to build a primate brain
space.body: Researchers in Taiwan and Japan found a small stretch of DNA that changes which brain-building cells are produced, helping explain how the primate neocortex expanded — evolution opened a new developmental path without creating entirely new genes. The work, led by National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University and Academia Sinica with Kyoto University, was published in Science Advances.

space.headline: A microbe-made molecule may reverse gut damage by boosting NAD
space.body: Rutgers Health scientists found a molecule made by “good” gut bacteria — N-methylnicotinamide, or N-MNA — that drives stem-cell renewal and repair of the gut lining in mice, flies and human cells, by replenishing NAD, a coenzyme whose decline is linked to inflammatory bowel disease and other chronic gut disorders. The study was published in Science Advances.

space.headline: A likely supermassive neutron star may fill the mass gap
space.body: Astronomers found a red giant star with an unseen companion that is likely an unusually massive neutron star — an estimated 2.2 solar masses, between 1.8 and 2.8 — pushing the boundary of how massive neutron stars can get and shedding light on the mass gap between neutron stars and black holes. The binary, J0008+0128, was identified in LAMOST and APOGEE data and reported in Science Advances.

apod.title: A Global Rebound for Mangroves
apod.credit: NASA Earth Observatory / Michala Garrison, using Landsat data from the U.S. Geological Survey
apod.explanation: After decades of decline, the world's mangrove forests are making a comeback. Research published in Science, based on Landsat imagery from 1984 to 2023, found mangroves lost nearly 3,000 square kilometres between 1984 and 2010, then gained back nearly 2,000 square kilometres after 2010 — led by Asia, Australia and South America. This Landsat view from February 2026 shows mangrove expansion in Palaw Township, Burma, where trees have regrown in abandoned rice fields and spread into new mudflats. Mangroves store up to four times as much carbon as taller inland tropical forests and shield coasts from erosion and storm surge.
